trace.title: Client network and identity
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

MSK provides managed Kafka options. It reduces parts of broker infrastructure work, but does not choose event keys, schemas, consumer groups, offset policy, or business idempotence for you.

Provisioned/serverless options have different configuration and capacity contracts.

A client needs reachable advertised broker endpoints, the selected authentication/TLS mechanism, authorization, and compatible client support. “The bootstrap server responds” is not enough if metadata returns endpoints the client cannot reach.

Setup: choose the MSK offering/version, private connectivity and access mechanism, topic/partition policy, client credentials/role support, monitoring, and retention. Run the local Kafka lab first.

Then test a synthetic event and replay in the chosen training AWS environment.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Client contacts bootstrap → discovers leaders → authenticates/connects to actual brokers → produces keyed record → group consumes/commits under its own policy. Debug network, auth, topic access, and business processing separately.

Retention and consumer downtime interact. A lagging consumer can lose required history after retention; managed brokers do not extend the business recovery window automatically.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail:
MSK does not make a Rails DB write and Kafka publish atomic. Client libraries can require explicit support for the selected authentication method.

A topic with one hot key can bottleneck despite more brokers.
